_howto: One shot per generation. Paste the shot's 'paste' value into Kling's main prompt box and the shot's 'negative' value into Kling's negative prompt box - they are separate fields and mixing them is what produces the thing you asked to avoid. Same model version, same mode, same seed for all eight. Camera movement: none/custom, never auto.

film.title: THE KEEPER
film.logline: A lighthouse keeper carrying a hand lamp up a dark tower discovers the light he tends has been out for weeks, and that nothing on the island has been waiting for him.
film.spine: He believes he is keeping the light. He is not, and has not been for a long time.
film.runtime: 40s at 5s per clip, ~55s if shots 3, 7 and 8 are run at 10s

shots.title: The tower is dark (establish)
shots.paste: Night on a black wet rock shelf above a heaving sea. A squat granite lighthouse forty feet tall, four tapering courses of grey unpainted stone, a black iron gallery rail beneath a green oxidised copper dome, one narrow black door at the base, three small stair windows up the shaft, no stripes and no paint. Every window is dark and the lamp room at the top is completely dark. Behind the three stair windows a single small amber flame climbs slowly from the lowest window to the highest, one window at a time. Nothing else in the frame moves except the sea. Camera: static locked-off extreme wide, 24mm, locked horizon, no camera movement, tower centred and small in frame. Lighting: no moon, overcast sky one stop brighter than the black sea, the only light source in frame is the small amber flame inside the tower, all stone falling to near black. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. Palette: wet slate grey, sodium amber, bone white, tidal green-black.

shots.title: The climb (establish)
shots.paste: Inside the lighthouse. The keeper, a heavy-set man in his sixties with grey stubble and wet flattened hair, wearing a black oilskin coat over a cream cable-knit sweater, no hat, climbs a narrow granite spiral stair carrying a brass hurricane lamp with a soot-blackened glass chimney at chest height, burning a small steady amber flame. Salt bloom on the curved stone wall, a black iron handrail. One event only: he climbs at an even unhurried pace, then stops on a step and listens. Camera: steady forward dolly following him up the spiral stair at walking pace, 28mm, one-point perspective up the stairwell, locked horizon. Lighting: single practical source, the hurricane lamp in his hand, no fill, extreme contrast, amber raking across wet granite, the stairwell above and below him fully black. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. Palette: wet slate grey, sodium amber, bone white, tidal green-black.

shots.title: The dead lens (escalate)
shots.paste: The lamp room at the top of the lighthouse. A huge Fresnel lens, a barrel of concentric glass rings taller than a man, stands in the centre furred with salt and grey dust. The keeper, a heavy-set man in his sixties with grey stubble and wet flattened hair, wearing a black oilskin coat over a cream cable-knit sweater, no hat, raises a brass hurricane lamp with a soot-blackened glass chimney toward it, the flame small and steady amber. The burner inside the lens is black and cold, the wick a stub of carbon. The glass returns a few dull amber glints and no beam. One event: he raises the lamp and the lens fails to catch. Camera: slow push-in, 50mm, focus racking from his face to the dead lens, ending with the lens filling the frame as a circle. Lighting: hurricane lamp from below and camera left, no fill, extreme contrast, deep shadow filling the top of the room, sea black beyond the gallery glass. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. shots.title: The same entry, again (escalate)
shots.paste: Close on a bare wooden table. An open logbook, its paper swollen and wavy with damp, a perfect dark ring of lamp soot printed on the page. The keeper's bare hand turns page after page after page, each page filled top to bottom with the same short line of handwriting in the same faded ink. The handwriting is unreadable ink strokes only, no legible words and no numbers, softening out of focus toward the edges of the page. One event: the hand turns pages, faster. Camera: static locked-off overhead close, 50mm, shallow depth of field, page edges soft. Lighting: hurricane lamp just out of frame camera right, hard raking amber across the paper grain, the rest of the room black. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. Palette: wet slate grey, sodium amber, bone white, tidal green-black.

shots.title: The crates (turn)
shots.paste: The narrow black door at the base of the granite lighthouse opens inward. The keeper, a heavy-set man in his sixties in a black oilskin coat over a cream cable-knit sweater, no hat, stands in the doorway holding a brass hurricane lamp with a soot-blackened glass chimney low at his hip, its amber flame guttering, so he reads as a black silhouette. Outside on the wet stone landing stage a stack of wooden supply crates sits unopened, lids still nailed down, rope handles swollen with rain and furred with green weed, the lowest crate collapsed and sprouting pale grass. One event: he stops in the doorway and does not step out. Camera: static locked-off medium wide from inside the doorway looking out, 35mm, locked horizon, no camera movement. Lighting: the hurricane lamp behind and below him so his figure reads fully black, weak amber spill reaching only the nearest crate, sea and sky beyond entirely black. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. Palette: wet slate grey, sodium amber, bone white, tidal green-black.

shots.title: Something passes unwarned (escalate)
shots.paste: The iron gallery outside the lamp room, high above the sea. The keeper, a heavy-set man in his sixties in a black oilskin coat over a cream cable-knit sweater, no hat, stands with his back to camera at the rail, a brass hurricane lamp with a soot-blackened glass chimney hanging at his side, its amber flame bent flat by the wind. Out in the dark two small bone-white lights slide past very close and low on the water, a large unlit hull passing unwarned. No beam reaches it. One event: the two lights cross the frame and go out behind the tower. Camera: slow lateral tracking shot moving against the direction the lights travel, 50mm, locked horizon. Lighting: keeper edge-lit amber down one side by his own lamp only, everything else black, the two passing lights as small bone-white points with no glow around them. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. shots.title: The match (rhyme with shot 3)
shots.paste: The lamp room at the top of the lighthouse, the huge Fresnel lens of concentric glass rings taller than a man in the centre. The keeper, a heavy-set man in his sixties with grey stubble and wet flattened hair, wearing a black oilskin coat over a cream cable-knit sweater, no hat, strikes a match at the cold burner inside the lens. The match catches and for a moment the concentric rings fill with hundreds of small reflections. In the curved glass behind him the stairwell reads as one tall vertical absence where the reflections do not appear. His brass hurricane lamp stands on the floor nearly out, the flame blue at the base. One event: the match catches. Camera: slow push-in, 50mm, focus racking from his face to the dead lens, ending with the lens filling the frame as a circle. Lighting: match flare as a small hard second source, bone white for one beat then falling back to amber, no fill, deep shadow, the vertical absence in the glass never lit. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. Palette: wet slate grey, sodium amber, bone white, tidal green-black.

shots.title: The light (pay off, rhyme with shot 1)
shots.paste: Night on a black wet rock shelf above a heaving sea. A squat granite lighthouse forty feet tall, four tapering courses of grey unpainted stone, a black iron gallery rail beneath a green oxidised copper dome, one narrow black door at the base, three small stair windows up the shaft, no stripes and no paint. The three stair windows are dark and empty, no amber flame anywhere inside the tower. The lamp room at the top fills with a cold mercury white-green light and one clean beam sweeps out across the water a single time, then holds, pointing away from camera. Nothing else in the frame moves except the sea. Camera: static locked-off extreme wide, 24mm, locked horizon, no camera movement, tower centred and small in frame. Lighting: no moon, overcast sky one stop brighter than the black sea, the only light source is the cold mercury white-green beam from the lamp room, granite lit hard along one edge and falling to black. Style: photographed live action, 35mm anamorphic, shallow depth of field, fine film grain, deep true blacks, no illustration and no rendering. _notes.anchor: The brass hurricane lamp in the keeper's hand is the only working light in the film. It runs a state clock: steady amber (1-3), low and guttering (4-5), bent flat by wind (6), nearly out and blue at the base (7), gone (8). The tower's own light is absent until the last shot.
_notes.palette_break: Cold mercury white-green appears only in shot 8. It is forbidden in shots 1-7 on purpose. Do not 'fix' it by grading it back to amber.
_notes.locked_strings: The tower description, the keeper description and the hurricane lamp description are repeated word-for-word in every shot that contains them. Do not paraphrase them between generations - paraphrasing is what makes the building change shape.
_notes.kling_settings: Same model version and same mode for all 8 shots. Fixed seed. Relevance/prompt-adherence high (creativity low). Camera movement set to none or custom, never auto. Negative prompt pasted into Kling's separate negative box, never into the main prompt.
_notes.audio: Kling's text-to-video path does not give you reliable native sound, so audio is built in the edit, not prompted. Bed: low sea swell and wind at constant level under every shot, one 30 Hz sub-bass drone entering at shot 4 and never leaving, dry close foley for footsteps on stone and page turns, absolute silence for half a second before shot 8's beam. No dialogue anywhere.
